text:
Alex: FYI I've been seeing a strange prefix mismatch when we hit KV eviction on the new quantized bring-up (4-bit).
Alex: Short repro attached below, failing intermittently on long sessions > 64k tokens.
Alex: ```
# run repro
python tests/kv_eviction_repro.py --model rdm-30b-q4 --seq 131072 --prefix-file long_prompt.txt
# observed: generation drifts right after eviction boundary (tokens diverge)
TRACE: kv-cache: evicting 8192 tokens at index 57344
TRACE: attention: rotary-scale applied with factor 1.0002 (quant path)
ERR: output mismatch at step 57350: expected token=" the", got=" a"
```
Alex: Anyone seen rotary/scale differences between fp kernels and quant kernels?
Sam: i looked briefly — we had one small change in the quant attention kernel where we clip positions to int16 to reduce memory. could that be it?
Sam: can you paste the small binary diff?
Alex: here's the kernel patch in question (from rdm-qkernel v0.9):
Alex: ```
- pos = (i - base) * scale_factor
+ pos = clamp((i - base) * scale_factor, -32768, 32767)
```
Maria: clamp sounds suspicious. RoPE relies on continuous phase; clamping positions will distort phase for large offsets.
Maria: is the model using RoPE frequency table that expects float64-style scaling?
Evan: I ran a tiny bisect overnight: float32 path vs q4 path. Float32 baseline is clean, q4 shows tiny phase drift accumulating around the eviction boundary.
Evan: Minimal repro I used: loop append random tokens until eviction, then compare attention keys. Small script:
Evan: ```
for step in range(60000):
  out_fp = model_fp.step(input)
  out_q = model_q.step(input)
  if diff(out_fp.kv, out_q.kv) > 1e-3:
     print('drift at', step)
     break
```
Evan: got drift at 57350 (same spot).
Sam: hmm. Could be quant rounding of the incremental position value before sinusoidal table lookup.
Maria: Another angle: check whether prefix eviction code reindexes correctly for quantized kv buffers. If we copy slices using int indices that overflow, we could be losing alignment.
Alex: Good call. In the repro logs the evicted index printed as 57344 which is exactly 0xE000 — near int16 negative wrap zone if mishandled.
Sam: ah, 0xE000 as signed int16 = -8192. If some code uses int16 for offsets, slice math might wrap.
Alex: That would explain clamp + wrap causing a tiny rotational phase offset.
Maria: Steps to confirm: 1) compare raw position indices written into kv buffers for fp vs q path, 2) compare sin/cos table lookups for those positions, 3) validate memcpy/slice code doesn't use int16 indexing.
Evan: I instrumented the q kernel to dump pos indices around eviction. Here's a snippet:
Evan: ```
KV_POS_DUMP: [57336, 57337, 57338, 57339, 57340, 57341, 57342, 57343, 57344, -8192, -8191, -8190, ...]
```
Evan: see that? after 57344 it wraps to -8192.
Alex: omg that's the bug. somewhere the index cast to int16 during the shift.
Sam: which file? I suspect the shared helper in runtime/kernels/pos_index.c uses int16_t for temporary to save mem.
Maria: if it's a temp we can change it to int32 and keep same mem for steady state. tests should pass.
Evan: Quick patch locally changed the temp to int32 and the drift disappeared on my bisect run.
Evan: Local test: no drift up to 131k tokens.
Alex: nice. Can you open a PR with the patch + a unit test that constructs a long prefix and forces eviction?
Evan: On it. I'll add a test that asserts raw pos values are monotonic and not negative after eviction.
Sam: also add a small fuzz harness to run both fp and q kernels for 1k random seeds so CI can catch regressions.
Alex: good idea. ci-bot: please run the nightly qkernel stress job once PR lands.
ci-bot: scheduled nightly job: rdm-qkernel-stress (runs 22:00 UTC).
Maria: one more thing — we should add a gating eval that compares downstream generation KL for long prompts between fp and q paths to catch silent drifts even if kv indices look OK.
Alex: agreed. I'll create an eval in the onboarding suite that runs a handful of long-context prompts and checks token-level agreement > 99.5%.
Sam: fine by me. PR review checklist: patch, unit test, fuzz harness, CI job added to YAML, and mention potential perf hit if we avoid int16. We'll benchmark impact.
Evan: perf diff is negligible on my microbench (0.3% CPU), probably fine.
Alex: thanks team. assigning follow-ups: Evan PR+tests, Sam add fuzz harness CI, Maria add gating eval, Alex coordinate release notes.
Evan: PR 5421 draft opened: https://git.redwood/rdm/qkernel/pull/5421
Alex: will merge after CI green. :thumbsup:
Maria: great catch — could have been nasty in-prod for long-running sessions.
Sam: TL;DR: int16 index wrap in quant kernel -> RoPE phase shift after KV eviction; patching to int32 fixes it.
Alex: closing loop when merged.
